Senses.Note: In the Extended Record of Yongjue Yuanxian, Yongjue quotes "gathering the mind is called restraint" (攝心名戒), then challenges it point by point: "what thing is mind that it can be gathered? What thing is gathering that it can gather mind? Water does not wash water" (心是何物而可攝？攝又是何物而可攝心？水不洗水). Yongming Yanshou's Source-Mirror Record states that before reaching its stated gate, "saying right makes wrong; gathering the mind is still an error" (說是成非，攝心猶錯). Shiwu Qinggong's community verse retains the ordinary finite action by listing chanting and "gathering the mind to drive off sleep" (攝心除睡). Counted forms include "gathering the mind is called restraint" (攝心名戒, two occurrences in two texts), "gather the mind to drive off sleep" (攝心除睡, two in two), "the way of gathering the mind" (攝心之法, one), "place of gathering the mind" (攝心處, one), and "gather the mind and illuminate within" (攝心內照, three in three). The entry records the action and the texts' own challenges without resolving those challenges into an external system.

gather the mind to drive off sleep (攝心除睡)
gathering the mind is called restraint (攝心名戒)
Senses.Explanation: Gathering the mind is the proposed finite action of collecting, drawing in, or holding in the mind. Chan records both give that action concrete work and challenge whether the wording has any stable basis: the tension belongs in the definition rather than being resolved into a system. The phrase occurs 137 times in 71 texts. Asked to ‘show the way of gathering the mind’ (示攝心之法), Chaozong Tongren answers, ‘sit still for one stick of incense’ (靜坐一爐香), but immediately calls this ‘a fine saying’ and warns that it must not be misunderstood (好箇話頭，只是不得錯會). In a separate verse requested on the term, Chaozong says, ‘the myriad things are brightly clear—what thought and what consideration? If you intend to gather the mind, there is no basis to rely on. I now write these words for you; just this is the place of gathering the mind’ (萬法朗然，何思何慮？擬欲攝心，無本可據……只此便是攝心處).

Occurrences.Kwic: 雲峯悅云：這僧雖然頭上有光，不知脚下似漆。直饒十字縱橫，朝打三千，暮打八百。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X83/X83n1578.xml). Record Pointing at the Moon (指月錄). Speaker: Yunfeng.

Occurrences.Kwic: 上堂：業鏡當臺，賊身已露。既是贓物現在，為什不肯招伏？會麼？朝打三千，暮打八百。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X82/X82n1571.xml). Complete Five Lamps (Vols. 34–120) (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)). Speaker: Baoning Renyong.

Occurrences.Kwic: 雲峰悅云：這僧頂上有光，不知脚下有漆，且作麼生會？直饒儞十字縱橫，朝打三千，暮打八百。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X79/X79n1557.xml). Essential Compendium of the United Lamp (聯燈會要). Speaker: Yunfeng.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師出世三十年，雖嚴冷孤峻，而又柔易雍和，室中騐人，不擅許可。故其椎拂之下，所得之士，類皆銅頭鐵額，能世其家者。生平所記，語錄之外，訓世羣集，總計三十種，近百卷，流布宇內。偶示疾，山神夜哭，樹木摧折，病中歌唱自娛。三月前，謂侍僧曰：我臨終須大喝而去。崇禎十二年己卯七月三十，索筆書偈曰：朝打三千，暮打八百，要會聚雲，眉毛出血。投筆危坐至午，果大喝一聲而逝。師壽五十有八，臘三十。闍維，煙至松󳱬，結為五彩荷香，徧地起骨，得黃金鎖子三莖，齒化為紫色，五色舍利三百餘顆，入土者無數。平都地藏院迎十二顆建塔，餘皆塔於本寺三目山之陽。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X84/X84n1583.xml). Orthodox Continuation of the Lamp (續燈正統). Speaker: Juyun Chuiwan Guangzhen.

Occurrences.Kwic: 脚踢須彌倒。浮生夢幻身，人命夕難保。天堂并地獄，皆由心所造。南山北嶺松，北嶺南山草。一雨潤無邊，根苗壯枯槁。五湖參學人，但問虗空討。死脫夏天衫，生披冬月襖。分明無事人，特地生煩惱。喝一喝，下座。上堂：一喝分賓主，照用一時行。要會箇中意，日午打三更。遂喝一喝，曰：且道是賓是主？還有分得者麼？若也分得，朝打三千，暮打八百。若也未能，老僧失利。因同道相訪，上堂：颯颯涼風景，同人訪寂寥。煑茶山上水，燒鼎洞中樵。珍重！問：達磨未來時如何？師曰：長安夜夜家家月。曰：來後如何？師曰：幾處笙歌幾處愁。問：一物不將來時如何？師曰：槐木成林。曰：四山火來時如何？師曰：物逐人興。曰：步步登高時如何？師曰：雲生足下。問：古人封白紙，意旨如何？師曰：家貧路富。問：如何是祖師西來意？師曰：三日風，五日雨。上堂：夫宗師
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X81/X81n1568.xml). Strict Lineage of the Five Lamps (Vols. 10–25) (五燈嚴統(第10卷-第25卷)). Speaker: Shishuang Chuyuan.

Senses.Explanation: Three thousand blows in the morning, eight hundred in the evening is a coordinated verdict prescribing repeated blows across the day. Both time clauses form the deployed saying. Ruoan Tongwen applies the full pair to a patriarch; Yunfeng repeats it as a verdict on an agile monk; Baoning Renyong uses it after exposing a culprit; Shishuang Chuyuan places it in a hall test; Juyun Chuiwan writes it in his final verse.
